newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar seen buoyant after G7 shake out.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar seen buoyant after G7 shake out.

text.p: Dollar/mark bulls should shake off Friday's bout of pre-G7 jitters and recover their nerve next week, chartists predicted.

"We remain bullish despite this selloff," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International. "It is predominately position squaring. If it stops right here it's all well and good."
The dollar reached a peak of 1.6755 marks on Friday before erasing all the day's gains, as traders squared up before Saturday's gathering of G7 finance ministers and central bankers in Berlin.
The confab promises to include a lively discussion on the strength of the dollar.

Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston said he is eyeing one-month trendline support, which comes in at 1.6465 on Friday and rises to 1.6505 on Monday, as a key pivot for dollar/mark.
"That is the point that needs to break to turn the intraday pullback into a much larger correction," he said.

Meanwhile other analysts were more cautious, saying the dollar's brush with new highs in dollar/mark came close to long-term objectives near 1.68, as did it's test of a new four-year top at 124.72 yen.
If the dollar ends below 1.6580 marks, near it's previous major top, it would be a neutral or even bearish event for dollar bulls, said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see the dollar go back up and test these highs," Johnson said. "But we need to get above 126 yen and 1.68 marks to get me bullish again in the bigger picture."
At 1600 EST on Friday, the dollar was trading at 1.6580/85 marks and 122.90/00 yen, down from 1.6670/75 marks and 124.20/25 yen at the U.S. open.
